title: How do we find all eight angles from one?
description: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one of the eight angles is given as one hundred and thirty five degrees. Corresponding and vertically opposite angles give three more of that size, and linear pairs give the other four. Keeko doubts the answer, because Keeko thinks all eight angles are alike.
teaching_notes: One idea: with parallel lines, every angle is either the given angle or its linear partner, so only two sizes appear. Watch for students who call all eight angles equal.

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle
video_script.why: The child chains corresponding, vertically opposite and linear pair facts to find every angle of the figure from one.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: parallel lines l and m, transversal t, angles one to four at l and five to eight at m, angle six is one hundred and thirty five degrees
video_script.anchor: parallel lines l and m cut by the transversal t, with angles 1 to 4 round the crossing with l and 5 to 8 in the same corners at m, and angle 6 marked 135°
video_script.wrong_answer: all eight angles are one hundred and thirty five
video_script.wrong_move: gives every angle the size of the given angle, because they look alike
video_script.payoff_line: Four angles are equal, and the other four are their linear partners

final_answer.value: Angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 are 135°; angles 1, 3, 5 and 7 are 45°
final_answer.spoken: angles two, four, six and eight are one hundred and thirty five degrees, and angles one, three, five and seven are forty five degrees

hold_back: Angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 are 135°; angles 1, 3, 5 and 7 are 45°
maths_rules: angle 2 is the corresponding angle of angle 6, so angle 2 = 135
angle 8 is vertically opposite to angle 6, so angle 8 = 135
angle 4 is the corresponding angle of angle 8, so angle 4 = 135
angles 5 and 6 are a linear pair, so angle 5 = 180 - 135 = 45
in the same way angles 1, 3 and 7 are 45
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video. Angles two, four, six and eight are filled in one colour, and angles one, three, five and seven in another as they are found.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all eight angles are one hundred and thirty five degrees, because they all look alike.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But angles five and six sit side by side on a straight line.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Two angles that add up to one hundred and eighty cannot both be one hundred and thirty five.
